security_audit.summary: Static findings were false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline Java identifiers, placeholder URLs, and sample webhook code. No prompt injection, hidden command execution, or unauthorized network destination was found. The only semantic concern is missing privacy guidance for recordings and caller input.

remediation.issue: Call recording and DTMF examples lack privacy guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance for caller consent, data retention, recording access controls, and handling sensitive caller input.

remediation.issue: Connection string examples use an access-key placeholder.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that secrets must stay in a secure secret store and never appear in prompts, logs, or source control.

content.user_title: Build Azure Call Automation in Java
content.value_statement: Java teams need clear patterns for automated calling, IVR, and media workflows. This skill provides focused Azure Communication Services examples for faster implementation.
actual_capabilities: Shows the Maven dependency for the Azure Communication Call Automation Java SDK.
Demonstrates client creation with DefaultAzureCredential and connection string options.
Provides examples for outbound calls, answering incoming calls, and call transfers.
Covers media playback with text-to-speech and hosted audio files.
Shows DTMF recognition, speech recognition, call recording, and webhook event parsing.
limitations: Does not provision Azure Communication Services resources or phone numbers.
Uses placeholder endpoints, callback URLs, users, and phone numbers.
Does not include complete authentication, deployment, or production monitoring setup.
Does not provide legal advice for call recording, consent, or telecom compliance.

use_cases.title: Prototype Java IVR flows
use_cases.description: Use the examples to design menus that play prompts and collect DTMF or speech input.

use_cases.title: Connect webhooks to call events
use_cases.description: Map Azure callback events to application logic for connected, recognized, playback, and disconnected states.

use_cases.title: Plan call recording features
use_cases.description: Review SDK operations for starting, pausing, resuming, stopping, and downloading call recordings.

prompt_templates.title: Create a simple setup plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline the steps for creating an Azure Communication Services Java call automation client.

prompt_templates.title: Design an IVR call flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a Java IVR flow that plays a greeting and collects DTMF input.

prompt_templates.title: Handle callback events
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to explain how a Java service should parse Azure Call Automation callback events.

prompt_templates.title: Review a production workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my Java call automation plan for recording, routing, media playback, and privacy controls.

output_examples.input: Design an IVR workflow for support calls.
output: Create the call automation client with Azure credentials.
Answer the incoming call from the callback context.
Collect DTMF input for menu selection.
Route the call based on the selected option.

output_examples.input: Explain how to handle callback events.
output: Parse the request body with the Azure event parser.
Handle connected events before starting media operations.
Process recognition results when callers finish input.
Log playback completion and disconnected events for operations.
Identify the server call identifier before starting recording.
Choose channel, content, and format settings.
Add controls for pause, resume, and stop actions.
Store recordings with access control and retention rules.

best_practices: Use managed identity or secure secret storage for Azure credentials and connection strings.
Validate callback authenticity and protect webhook endpoints before processing call events.
Add consent, retention, and access controls before enabling recording or sensitive input collection.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode real phone numbers, access keys, callback secrets, or recording URLs in source control.
Do not collect account numbers or speech input without clear purpose and protection.
Do not treat sample snippets as a complete production architecture.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build Java workflows for Azure Communication Services Call Automation, including IVR, callbacks, media, and recording.

faq.question: Does it create Azure resources?
faq.answer: No. It explains Java SDK usage and expects existing Azure Communication Services resources.

faq.question: Can it help with incoming calls?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes an example for answering incoming calls from an Event Grid callback context.

faq.question: Does it cover speech and DTMF recognition?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows examples for collecting DTMF tones and using speech recognition prompts.

faq.question: Does it include production security controls?
faq.answer: No. Add authentication, webhook validation, secret storage, monitoring, and privacy controls for production use.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible skill workflows.
